questions.question: Q: What is the difference between analysis and evaluation?

points.text: Analysis explains how and why choreographic choices work; evaluation judges how effective they are — analysis is about understanding, evaluation is about judging success.

questions.question: Q: Why must evaluation be supported by evidence?

points.text: Evidence grounds your judgement in fact; without it, evaluation is mere opinion and gains no marks in the AQA exam.

questions.question: Q: Give two criteria you could use to evaluate a dance work.

points.text: Clarity of intention (how clearly the purpose is communicated) and cohesion (how well the elements work together as a unified whole).

questions.question: Q: How would you evaluate a section of a dance as partially effective?

points.text: State what works well with evidence, then explain what is less successful with evidence — for example, 'the lift effectively shows trust but the transition into it is unclear, weakening the overall impact.'

questions.question: Q: Why is it important to evaluate your own choreography honestly?

points.text: Honest evaluation identifies genuine strengths and areas for improvement, showing the examiner mature reflective practice rather than uncritical self-praise.
